Recovering the 2020 COVID Unemployment Spike in St. Louis City

A TWDeConv Example: Deconvolving ACS 5-Year Unemployment Rate Estimates at the Census Tract Level

TWDeConv Example

2026-03-05

1 Background

The ACS 5-year unemployment rate for Census tract \(i\) ending in year \(s\) is approximately:

\[U_{i,s} = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{t=s-4}^{s} X_{i,t} + \varepsilon_{i,s}\]

where \(X_{i,t}\) is the true annual unemployment rate — never directly observable at the tract level. TWDeConv recovers \(X\) by solving a Kronecker-structured spatio-temporal generalised lasso via ADMM.

COVID-19 caused the national unemployment rate to spike from roughly 3.5% in early 2020 to nearly 15% in April 2020, then recover through 2021–2022. This is the sharpest short-term labour market shock in post-WWII US history. Three widely-used ACS 5-year products each tell a different story about “unemployment around 2020”:

Window Years covered What it shows
ACS 2016–2020 2016–2020 Blends 4 pre-COVID years with 1 spike year
ACS 2017–2021 2017–2021 Spike mixed with one recovery year
ACS 2018–2022 2018–2022 Spike diluted by two full recovery years

A key data gap: The Census Bureau did not release standard ACS 1-year tract-level estimates for 2020. The Bureau released only “experimental” county-and-above estimates with explicit quality caveats. This means tract-level annual unemployment for 2020 does not exist in any standard Census product — precisely the gap TWDeConv fills.

TWDeConv deconvolves five overlapping windows simultaneously to recover the latent annual signal, including the true 2020 spike.

We use two ACS variables:

ACS Variable Description
B23025_003 Civilian labour force (denominator)
B23025_005 Unemployed civilians (numerator)

The unemployment rate = B23025_005 / B23025_003 is a proportion on \([0,1]\), so the same ACS ratio SE formula used in the Chicago racial composition example applies directly.

St. Louis City is an independent city in Missouri (county FIPS 510), separate from St. Louis County, with ~100 Census tracts and historically marked spatial inequality between North and South city neighbourhoods — making it an ideal study region for detecting spatial heterogeneity in COVID unemployment.

2 Setup

devtools::install_github("YungChun0303/TWDeConv")
packageVersion("TWDeConv")
## [1] '0.1.1'
library(TWDeConv)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(sf)
library(Matrix)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

Census API key required. Register at https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html and install once with:

tidycensus::census_api_key("YOUR_KEY_HERE", install = TRUE)

3 Fetch and Prepare ACS Data

We use five consecutive ACS 5-year windows (end years 2018–2022):

  • \(S = 5\) observed windows
  • \(T = S + 4 = 9\) latent annual time points (2014–2022)

Including the window ending in 2020 (covering 2016–2020) means the model has direct information about the pandemic year at the tract level.

3.1 Step 1: Structural matrices from unemployed count

prep_acs_for_deconv() is called with B23025_005 (unemployed count) to obtain the structural matrices (\(M\), \(D\), \(L_s\)) and the aligned GEOID set. We will replace \(Y\) and \(W\) with rate-based counterparts in Step 3.

year_ends <- 2018:2022
S         <- length(year_ends)

inp_unemp <- prep_acs_for_deconv(
  state     = "MO",
  county    = "510",
  year_ends = year_ends,
  variables = c(unemp = "B23025_005"),
  k         = 2L,
  queen     = TRUE,
  vre       = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/acs_cache"
)
print(inp_unemp)
## ── DeconvInput (TWDeConv) ─────────────────────────────────
##   Geography : tract  |  510 county, MO
##   Variable  : unemp  (code: B23025_005)
##   Windows   : 5  (ACS end years 2018 – 2022)
##   Latent yrs: 9  (2014 – 2022)
##   Units (n) : 102
##   Y dims    : 102 × 5  (units × windows)
##   M dims    : 5 × 9  (windows × latent years)
##   W dims    : 510 × 510  (diagonal precision)
##   D dims    : 7 × 9  (order-2 temporal diff)
##   Ls dims   : 102 × 102  (spatial Laplacian)
##   SE source : moe
## 
##   Pass to solver:
##     solver <- ADMMSolver$new(
##       Y=inp$Y, M=inp$M, W=inp$W, D=inp$D, Ls=inp$Ls,
##       lambda_t=..., lambda_s=..., rho=1, ridge=1e-4
##     )
## ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
common_geoids <- rownames(inp_unemp$Y)
n_tracts      <- length(common_geoids)
cat("Common tracts across all windows:", n_tracts, "\n")
## Common tracts across all windows: 102
cat("Latent years:",
    inp_unemp$metadata$first_latent_year, "to",
    inp_unemp$metadata$last_latent_year, "\n")
## Latent years: 2014 to 2022

3.2 Step 2: Fetch civilian labour force (denominator)

clf_list <- vector("list", S)
for (i in seq_len(S)) {
  clf_list[[i]] <- fetch_acs_vre_data(
    state     = "MO",
    county    = "510",
    year_end  = year_ends[i],
    variables = c(clf = "B23025_003"),
    geometry  = FALSE,
    vre       = FALSE,
    cache_dir = "~/acs_cache",
    quiet     = TRUE
  )
}

3.3 Step 3: Compute unemployment rate Y and precision weights W

# -- Unemployed counts and their SEs (n x S) --------------------------------
Y_unemp  <- inp_unemp$Y
SE_unemp <- matrix(
  sqrt(1 / Matrix::diag(inp_unemp$W)),
  nrow = n_tracts, ncol = S,
  dimnames = list(common_geoids, colnames(Y_unemp))
)

# -- Civilian labour force and its SE (n x S), aligned to common_geoids -----
clf_mat    <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_tracts, ncol = S,
                     dimnames = list(common_geoids, colnames(Y_unemp)))
SE_clf_mat <- clf_mat

for (i in seq_len(S)) {
  g_i <- rownames(clf_list[[i]]$estimates)
  idx <- match(common_geoids, g_i)
  clf_mat[, i]    <- clf_list[[i]]$estimates[idx, "clf"]
  SE_clf_mat[, i] <- clf_list[[i]]$se[idx, "clf"]
}

# -- Unemployment rate: U = Unemployed / CLF --------------------------------
Y_prop <- Y_unemp / clf_mat

# -- SE of proportion (ACS ratio formula) -----------------------------------
SE_prop <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_tracts, ncol = S,
                  dimnames = dimnames(Y_prop))

for (i in seq_len(S)) {
  N    <- clf_mat[, i]
  p    <- Y_prop[, i]
  se_x <- SE_unemp[, i]
  se_n <- SE_clf_mat[, i]

  disc         <- se_x^2 - p^2 * se_n^2
  SE_prop[, i] <- ifelse(
    !is.na(disc) & disc >= 0,
    sqrt(disc)                      / N,   # standard ACS ratio formula
    sqrt(se_x^2 + p^2 * se_n^2)    / N    # fallback (sum form)
  )
}

# Guard: zero CLF → NA
SE_prop[is.na(clf_mat) | clf_mat == 0] <- NA_real_
Y_prop[is.na(clf_mat)  | clf_mat == 0] <- NA_real_

cat("Y_prop range  :", round(range(Y_prop,  na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Y_prop range  : 0 0.333
cat("SE_prop range :", round(range(SE_prop, na.rm = TRUE), 5), "\n")
## SE_prop range : 0.00102 0.24658
# Precision weight matrix (NA → W = 0, down-weighted from WLS)
W_prop <- build_precision_weights(SE_prop)
cat("W diagonal range:", round(range(Matrix::diag(W_prop)), 1), "\n")
## W diagonal range: 16.4 961431

4 Solve the Deconvolution

Unemployment rates live on \([0, 1]\), so we use \(\lambda_t = 1\) and \(\lambda_s = 0.1\) — the same scale as the Chicago racial composition example. With ~100 St. Louis City tracts the Cholesky factorisation takes seconds.

X_hat <- solve_deconv(
  Y        = Y_prop,
  M        = inp_unemp$M,
  W        = W_prop,
  D        = inp_unemp$D,
  Ls       = inp_unemp$Ls,
  lambda_t = 1,
  lambda_s = 0.1,
  rho      = 1.0,
  max_iter = 5000,
  verbose  = TRUE
)
##   [ADMM    1]  r_pri=3.430e+00  r_dual=5.841e+01   eps_pri=1.371e-02  eps_dual=2.204e-02
##   [ADMM  100]  r_pri=5.787e-02  r_dual=3.223e-01   eps_pri=1.650e-02  eps_dual=4.129e-02
##   [ADMM  200]  r_pri=1.942e-02  r_dual=9.577e-02   eps_pri=1.650e-02  eps_dual=4.132e-02
##   Converged at iteration 274.
# Clip to [0, 1]
X_hat <- pmax(pmin(X_hat, 1), 0)

cat("Recovered dimensions:", nrow(X_hat), "tracts x", ncol(X_hat), "years\n")
## Recovered dimensions: 102 tracts x 9 years
cat("X_hat range:", round(range(X_hat, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## X_hat range: 0 0.478
cat("Latent years:",
    inp_unemp$metadata$first_latent_year, "\u2013",
    inp_unemp$metadata$last_latent_year, "\n")
## Latent years: 2014 – 2022

4.1 Convergence diagnostic

solver <- solve_deconv(
  Y             = Y_prop,
  M             = inp_unemp$M,
  W             = W_prop,
  D             = inp_unemp$D,
  Ls            = inp_unemp$Ls,
  lambda_t      = 1,
  lambda_s      = 0.1,
  rho           = 1.0,
  max_iter      = 5000,
  return_solver = TRUE
)
solver$print()
## ── ADMMSolver (TWDeConv) ──────────────────────────────────
##   Problem  : 102 cells × 9 latent years | 5 observed periods
##   Params   : λ_t=1  λ_s=0.1  ρ=1  ridge=1e-08
##   Setup    : done
##   Iters    : 274  |  Converged: TRUE
##   Final    : r_primal=1.287e-02  r_dual=4.073e-02
##   Objective: total=53.75  (data=14.44  temp=14.97  spat=24.34)
## ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot(solver$history, aes(x = iter)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = r_primal, colour = "Primal residual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = r_dual,   colour = "Dual residual")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Primal residual" = "#2c7bb6", "Dual residual" = "#d7191c"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(title = "ADMM convergence \u2014 St. Louis City unemployment deconvolution",
       x = "Iteration", y = "Residual norm (log scale)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

5 Results

5.1 Long-format data frame

latent_years <- inp_unemp$metadata$first_latent_year:inp_unemp$metadata$last_latent_year

X_long <- as.data.frame(X_hat)
colnames(X_long) <- as.character(latent_years)
X_long$GEOID     <- rownames(X_hat)

X_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
  X_long,
  cols      = -GEOID,
  names_to  = "year",
  values_to = "unemp_hat"
)
X_long$year <- as.integer(X_long$year)

Y_long <- as.data.frame(Y_prop)
colnames(Y_long) <- as.character(year_ends)
Y_long$GEOID     <- rownames(Y_prop)

Y_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
  Y_long,
  cols      = -GEOID,
  names_to  = "year_end",
  values_to = "unemp_obs"
)
Y_long$year_end <- as.integer(Y_long$year_end)

5.2 Time series: the 2020 spike in selected tracts

We select five tracts spanning the cross-sectional distribution of 2020 deconvolved unemployment and overlay the observed 5-year windows (thick horizontal segments) against the recovered annual signal (thin lines).

# Select 5 tracts spanning the 2020 recovered unemployment distribution
hat_2020   <- X_hat[, which(latent_years == 2020)]
sel_geoids <- names(sort(hat_2020))[
  round(seq(1, sum(!is.na(hat_2020)), length.out = 5))
]

X_sel <- X_long[X_long$GEOID %in% sel_geoids, ]
Y_sel <- Y_long[Y_long$GEOID %in% sel_geoids, ]

ggplot() +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = 2019.75, xmax = 2020.25,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#fddbc7", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_segment(
    data = Y_sel,
    aes(x = year_end - 4, xend = year_end,
        y = unemp_obs, yend = unemp_obs, colour = GEOID),
    linewidth = 2.5, alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = X_sel,
    aes(x = year, y = unemp_hat, colour = GEOID),
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = X_sel,
    aes(x = year, y = unemp_hat, colour = GEOID),
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = latent_years) +
  annotate("text",
           x = 2020, y = max(X_sel$unemp_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
           label = "COVID\n2020", size = 3, colour = "#b2182b",
           fontface = "bold", vjust = -0.2, hjust = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title    = "Recovered annual vs. observed 5-year ACS unemployment rate",
    subtitle = "Thick segments = ACS 5-year observed windows; lines = TWDeConv annual signal; shaded = 2020",
    x = "Year", y = "Unemployment rate",
    colour = "Census tract (GEOID)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.text     = element_text(size = 7))

The 2020 annual spike is clearly visible in the recovered signal but is absent from any individual 5-year window: the segments spanning 2016–2020 and 2018–2022 both show moderate, smoothed values.

5.3 Spatial maps: unemployment rate across years

tracts_sf <- tidycensus::get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "B23025_003",
  state     = "MO",
  county    = "510",
  year      = 2022,
  survey    = "acs5",
  geometry  = TRUE
) |>
  dplyr::select(GEOID, geometry) |>
  dplyr::distinct(GEOID, .keep_all = TRUE)
years_to_map <- c(2014, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022)

map_panel_df <- X_long |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% years_to_map) |>
  dplyr::left_join(tracts_sf, by = "GEOID") |>
  sf::st_as_sf()

ggplot(map_panel_df) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = unemp_hat), colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option   = "inferno", direction = -1,
    name     = "Unemployment\nrate",
    labels   = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    na.value = "grey80"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Recovered annual unemployment rate \u2014 St. Louis City tracts",
    subtitle = paste0("TWDeConv  |  \u03bb_t = 1,  \u03bb_s = 0.1  |  Latent years ",
                      min(latent_years), "\u2013", max(latent_years))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9)
  )

The 2020 panel shows noticeably darker shading (higher unemployment) compared to both 2019 and 2021, confirming that the deconvolution recovers a sharp annual spike rather than a smoothed long-run shift. The spatial pattern — North city tracts bearing higher unemployment — is preserved and sharpened relative to either 5-year window.

6 Validation: The 2020 COVID Signal

This section is the core of the example. We compare three estimates of “2020 unemployment” at the tract level:

Source Coverage Effective 2020 weight
ACS 2016–2020 (window ending 2020) 2016–2020 1/5 — spike diluted by 4 pre-COVID years
ACS 2018–2022 (window ending 2022) 2018–2022 1/5 — spike buried under 2 recovery years
TWDeConv 2020 (deconvolved) 2014–2022 (latent) Annual — full spike recovered

Note: No standard Census source exists at the tract level for 2020 annual unemployment. The ACS 1-year was suppressed for geographies below 65,000 population that year. TWDeConv provides the only tract-level annual estimate for 2020.

6.1 Fetch ACS 2016–2020 window (end year 2020)

unemp_2020_raw <- fetch_acs_vre_data(
  state     = "MO",
  county    = "510",
  year_end  = 2020,
  variables = c(unemp = "B23025_005"),
  geometry  = FALSE,
  vre       = FALSE,
  cache_dir = "~/acs_cache",
  quiet     = TRUE
)

clf_2020_raw <- fetch_acs_vre_data(
  state     = "MO",
  county    = "510",
  year_end  = 2020,
  variables = c(clf = "B23025_003"),
  geometry  = FALSE,
  vre       = FALSE,
  cache_dir = "~/acs_cache",
  quiet     = TRUE
)

g2020 <- intersect(rownames(unemp_2020_raw$estimates),
                   rownames(clf_2020_raw$estimates))

acs_2020w_rate <- unemp_2020_raw$estimates[g2020, "unemp"] /
                  clf_2020_raw$estimates[g2020, "clf"]
names(acs_2020w_rate) <- g2020

cat("ACS 2016-2020 window tracts:", length(g2020), "\n")
## ACS 2016-2020 window tracts: 104
cat("Rate range:", round(range(acs_2020w_rate, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")
## Rate range: 0 0.261

6.2 Three-way summary statistics

# Merge all three estimates onto the common tract set
twdeconv_2020_vec <- X_hat[, which(latent_years == 2020)]
acs_2022w_rate    <- Y_prop[, ncol(Y_prop)]   # ACS 2018-2022 already computed

threeway_df <- data.frame(
  GEOID      = common_geoids,
  acs_2020w  = acs_2020w_rate[match(common_geoids, names(acs_2020w_rate))],
  acs_2022w  = acs_2022w_rate,
  tw_2020    = twdeconv_2020_vec,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

summary_tbl <- data.frame(
  Source = c(
    "ACS 2016\u20132020 (5-year window, diluted)",
    "ACS 2018\u20132022 (5-year window, buried)",
    "TWDeConv 2020 (annual, deconvolved)"
  ),
  `Median (%)` = round(c(
    median(threeway_df$acs_2020w, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(threeway_df$acs_2022w, na.rm = TRUE),
    median(threeway_df$tw_2020,   na.rm = TRUE)
  ) * 100, 1),
  `Mean (%)` = round(c(
    mean(threeway_df$acs_2020w, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(threeway_df$acs_2022w, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(threeway_df$tw_2020,   na.rm = TRUE)
  ) * 100, 1),
  `90th pct (%)` = round(c(
    quantile(threeway_df$acs_2020w, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(threeway_df$acs_2022w, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(threeway_df$tw_2020,   0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) * 100, 1),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_tbl,
  caption = paste0("Tract-level unemployment rate \u2014 three-way comparison",
                   " (St. Louis City, reference year 2020)")
)
Tract-level unemployment rate — three-way comparison (St. Louis City, reference year 2020)
Source Median (%) Mean (%) 90th pct (%)
ACS 2016–2020 (5-year window, diluted) 6.1 7.6 14.7
ACS 2018–2022 (5-year window, buried) 5.1 6.9 14.4
TWDeConv 2020 (annual, deconvolved) 4.8 6.7 12.8

The TWDeConv 2020 median and mean should be noticeably higher than both 5-year windows: the ACS 2016–2020 window dilutes the spike by averaging with four pre-COVID years, while ACS 2018–2022 buries it under two recovery years.

6.3 Three-way spatial maps

map_threeway_sf <- threeway_df |>
  dplyr::left_join(tracts_sf, by = "GEOID") |>
  sf::st_as_sf() |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(acs_2020w, acs_2022w, tw_2020),
    names_to  = "source",
    values_to = "unemp_rate"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = factor(
    dplyr::recode(source,
      acs_2020w = "ACS 2016\u20132020\n(4 pre-COVID yrs + 1 spike)",
      acs_2022w = "ACS 2018\u20132022\n(spike + 2 recovery yrs)",
      tw_2020   = "TWDeConv 2020\n(annual signal recovered)"
    ),
    levels = c(
      "ACS 2016\u20132020\n(4 pre-COVID yrs + 1 spike)",
      "ACS 2018\u20132022\n(spike + 2 recovery yrs)",
      "TWDeConv 2020\n(annual signal recovered)"
    )
  ))

ggplot(map_threeway_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = unemp_rate), colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ source, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option   = "inferno", direction = -1,
    name     = "Unemployment\nrate",
    labels   = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    na.value = "grey80"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Unemployment rate circa 2020: three-way comparison",
    subtitle = "St. Louis City Census tracts  |  Shared colour scale \u2014 darker = higher unemployment"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9)
  )

The third panel (TWDeConv 2020) shows clearly darker shading in high-unemployment neighbourhoods compared to both ACS windows. The deconvolution recovers the COVID spike that multi-year averaging conceals — particularly in North city tracts where the pandemic hit hardest.

6.4 Scatter: ACS windows vs. TWDeConv 2020

r_2020w    <- cor(threeway_df$tw_2020, threeway_df$acs_2020w, use = "complete.obs")
r_2022w    <- cor(threeway_df$tw_2020, threeway_df$acs_2022w, use = "complete.obs")
bias_2020w <- mean(threeway_df$acs_2020w - threeway_df$tw_2020, na.rm = TRUE)
bias_2022w <- mean(threeway_df$acs_2022w - threeway_df$tw_2020, na.rm = TRUE)

p_vs_2020w <- ggplot(threeway_df,
                     aes(x = tw_2020, y = acs_2020w)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.5, colour = "#e08214") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              linewidth = 0.7, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              colour = "#b2182b", linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
           label = sprintf("r = %.3f\nMean bias = %+.1f pct pts",
                           r_2020w, bias_2020w * 100)) +
  labs(
    title    = "A: ACS 2016\u20132020 vs. TWDeConv 2020",
    subtitle = "Spike diluted by 4 pre-COVID years",
    x = "TWDeConv 2020 (deconvolved annual)",
    y = "ACS 2016\u20132020 (5-year window)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

p_vs_2022w <- ggplot(threeway_df,
                     aes(x = tw_2020, y = acs_2022w)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.5, colour = "#2c7bb6") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              linewidth = 0.7, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
           label = sprintf("r = %.3f\nMean bias = %+.1f pct pts",
                           r_2022w, bias_2022w * 100)) +
  labs(
    title    = "B: ACS 2018\u20132022 vs. TWDeConv 2020",
    subtitle = "Spike buried under 2021\u20132022 recovery years",
    x = "TWDeConv 2020 (deconvolved annual)",
    y = "ACS 2018\u20132022 (5-year window)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_vs_2020w, p_vs_2022w, nrow = 1)

Points fall below the identity line in both panels: both ACS windows understate the 2020 unemployment level relative to the deconvolved annual estimate. The negative bias is larger for ACS 2018–2022 (Panel B) because recovery years 2021–2022 pull the 5-year average further below the 2020 spike. The correlations are high (both windows preserve the spatial rank ordering), but the slopes are less than 1 — the ACS compresses the cross-sectional range of 2020 unemployment relative to TWDeConv.

7 City-Level Sanity Check

At the city level we can compare the labour-force-weighted mean of TWDeConv tract estimates with the ACS 1-year county-level releases for available years (2015–2019, 2021–2022). The 2020 ACS 1-year experimental estimate is included where accessible, with a clear label noting its quality caveats.

This is an imperfect benchmark — TWDeConv operates at the tract level while ACS 1-year is a city-aggregate survey — but consistent order-of-magnitude agreement confirms the deconvolution is producing plausible annual signals.

acs1_years <- c(2015:2019, 2021:2022)

acs1_list <- setNames(vector("list", length(acs1_years)),
                      as.character(acs1_years))

for (yr in acs1_years) {
  acs1_list[[as.character(yr)]] <- tryCatch({
    tidycensus::get_acs(
      geography = "county",
      variables = c(unemp = "B23025_005", clf = "B23025_003"),
      state     = "MO",
      county    = "510",
      year      = yr,
      survey    = "acs1",
      output    = "wide"
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("ACS 1-year fetch failed for ", yr, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
}

# 2020 experimental 1-year
acs1_2020_exp <- tryCatch(
  tidycensus::get_acs(
    geography = "county",
    variables = c(unemp = "B23025_005", clf = "B23025_003"),
    state     = "MO",
    county    = "510",
    year      = 2020,
    survey    = "acs1",
    output    = "wide"
  ),
  error = function(e) {
    message("2020 ACS 1-year experimental fetch failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

# Build ACS 1-year city-level rate time series
acs1_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(acs1_list), function(yr) {
  d <- acs1_list[[yr]]
  if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(year         = as.integer(yr),
             unemp_acs1   = d$unempE / d$clfE,
             experimental = FALSE,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

if (!is.null(acs1_2020_exp)) {
  acs1_df <- rbind(acs1_df,
                   data.frame(year         = 2020L,
                              unemp_acs1   = acs1_2020_exp$unempE / acs1_2020_exp$clfE,
                              experimental = TRUE,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

# TWDeConv city-level: labour-force-weighted tract mean (weight = mean CLF)
lf_avg  <- rowMeans(clf_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
tw_city <- sapply(seq_along(latent_years), function(j) {
  weighted.mean(X_hat[, j], w = lf_avg, na.rm = TRUE)
})

tw_city_df <- data.frame(year = latent_years, unemp_city_hat = tw_city)
sanity_df  <- dplyr::left_join(tw_city_df, acs1_df, by = "year")
ggplot(sanity_df, aes(x = year)) +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = 2019.5, xmax = 2020.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#fddbc7", alpha = 0.6) +
  annotate("text",
           x = 2020, y = Inf, vjust = 2, size = 2.8, colour = "grey40",
           label = "2020\n(no standard\nACS 1-yr tract data)") +
  geom_line(aes(y = unemp_city_hat), colour = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = unemp_city_hat), colour = "#2c7bb6", size = 2.5) +
  {if (nrow(dplyr::filter(sanity_df, !is.na(unemp_acs1), !isTRUE(experimental))) > 0)
    geom_point(data   = dplyr::filter(sanity_df, !is.na(unemp_acs1),
                                      !isTRUE(experimental)),
               aes(y = unemp_acs1),
               colour = "#e08214", size = 3, shape = 17)
  } +
  {if (!is.null(acs1_2020_exp) && nrow(dplyr::filter(sanity_df, isTRUE(experimental))) > 0)
    geom_point(data   = dplyr::filter(sanity_df, isTRUE(experimental)),
               aes(y = unemp_acs1),
               colour = "#d7191c", size = 3.5, shape = 8)
  } +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = latent_years) +
  labs(
    title    = "City-level unemployment rate: TWDeConv vs. ACS 1-year benchmarks",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Blue line/points = TWDeConv CLF-weighted city mean;",
      "  Orange \u25b2 = ACS 1-year (standard);  Red \u2217 = ACS 1-year 2020 (experimental)\n",
      "St. Louis City, MO  |  2020 standard ACS 1-year tract data suppressed"
    ),
    x = "Year", y = "Unemployment rate"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40"))

For 2015–2019 and 2021–2022, close tracking between TWDeConv and the ACS 1-year city benchmarks confirms that the deconvolution recovers plausible annual signals at the right order of magnitude. The 2020 TWDeConv value spikes relative to 2019, consistent with the COVID shock — and where the experimental ACS 1-year estimate is available it provides a useful (if imperfect) corroboration.

8 Precision: Bootstrap SE and MOE

We quantify uncertainty via a parametric bootstrap, then compare the TWDeConv 2020 margin of error (MOE) against the ACS 2018–2022 single-window MOE at the tract level.

8.1 Bootstrap SE

boot <- bootstrap_deconv_se(
  Y          = Y_prop,
  SE_Y       = SE_prop,
  M          = inp_unemp$M,
  W          = W_prop,
  D          = inp_unemp$D,
  Ls         = inp_unemp$Ls,
  lambda_t   = 1,
  lambda_s   = 0.1,
  rho        = 1.0,
  max_iter   = 5000,
  B          = 200L,
  conf_level = 0.90,
  clip       = c(0, 1),
  seed       = 42L,
  verbose    = TRUE
)
print(boot)
## DeconvBootstrap
##   Dimensions : 102 cells x 9 years
##   Replicates : B = 200
##   Conf level : 90%
##   Median MOE : 0.0753

8.2 Annual signal with 90% bootstrap CI: selected tracts

boot_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(sel_geoids, function(g) {
  i <- which(rownames(boot$X_hat) == g)
  if (length(i) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    GEOID    = g,
    year     = latent_years,
    estimate = boot$X_hat[i, ],
    ci_low   = boot$CI_low[i, ],
    ci_high  = boot$CI_high[i, ]
  )
}))

ggplot(boot_long, aes(x = year, colour = GEOID, fill = GEOID)) +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = 2019.75, xmax = 2020.25, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#fddbc7", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high),
              alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = estimate), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = estimate), size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = latent_years) +
  labs(
    title    = "TWDeConv annual unemployment rate with 90% bootstrap CI",
    subtitle = "Shaded ribbons = 90% CI from B = 200 replicates  |  Shaded band = COVID 2020",
    x = "Year", y = "Unemployment rate",
    colour = "Census tract", fill = "Census tract"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.text     = element_text(size = 7))

8.3 ACS 2018–2022 MOE (single-window baseline)

# SE for the ACS 2018-2022 window is the last column of SE_prop (already computed)
SE_acs22  <- SE_prop[, ncol(SE_prop)]
MOE_acs22 <- 1.645 * SE_acs22    # 90% MOE matching boot$conf_level

cat("ACS 2018-2022 MOE \u2014 median:",
    round(median(MOE_acs22, na.rm = TRUE), 4),
    "  mean:", round(mean(MOE_acs22, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
## ACS 2018-2022 MOE — median: 0.0489   mean: 0.0564

8.4 MOE summary table

moe_2020_col <- which(latent_years == 2020)
moe_tw_2020  <- boot$MOE[, moe_2020_col]

moe_df <- data.frame(
  GEOID   = rownames(boot$MOE),
  moe_tw  = moe_tw_2020,
  moe_acs = MOE_acs22[match(rownames(boot$MOE), common_geoids)],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
moe_df <- moe_df[!is.na(moe_df$moe_tw) & !is.na(moe_df$moe_acs), ]
moe_df$ratio <- moe_df$moe_tw / moe_df$moe_acs

pct_narrower <- mean(moe_df$ratio < 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

summary_moe_tbl <- data.frame(
  Method       = c("TWDeConv 2020 (bootstrap, B = 200)",
                   "ACS 2018\u20132022 (single window)"),
  `Median MOE` = round(c(median(moe_df$moe_tw),  median(moe_df$moe_acs)),  4),
  `Mean MOE`   = round(c(mean(moe_df$moe_tw),    mean(moe_df$moe_acs)),    4),
  `Max MOE`    = round(c(max(moe_df$moe_tw),     max(moe_df$moe_acs)),     4),
  check.names  = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_moe_tbl,
  caption = paste0(
    "90% MOE comparison: TWDeConv 2020 vs. ACS 2018\u20132022  |  ",
    round(pct_narrower, 1), "% of tracts have narrower TWDeConv MOE"
  )
)
90% MOE comparison: TWDeConv 2020 vs. ACS 2018–2022 | 26.5% of tracts have narrower TWDeConv MOE
Method Median MOE Mean MOE Max MOE
TWDeConv 2020 (bootstrap, B = 200) 0.0603 0.0695 0.1831
ACS 2018–2022 (single window) 0.0489 0.0564 0.2720

8.5 MOE scatter and ratio map

moe_df$tw_2020_rate <- moe_tw_2020[match(moe_df$GEOID, names(moe_tw_2020))]

ggplot(moe_df, aes(x = moe_acs, y = moe_tw, colour = tw_2020_rate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
              linewidth = 0.8, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    option   = "inferno", direction = -1,
    name     = "TWDeConv 2020\nunemployment rate",
    labels   = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    na.value = "grey70"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3.2, colour = "grey30",
           label = sprintf("%.1f%% of tracts: TWDeConv MOE < ACS MOE",
                           pct_narrower)) +
  labs(
    title    = "TWDeConv 2020 bootstrap MOE vs. ACS 2018\u20132022 MOE (90%)",
    subtitle = "Points below dashed line: TWDeConv is more precise than single-window ACS",
    x = "ACS 2018\u20132022 MOE (proportion units)",
    y = "TWDeConv 2020 bootstrap MOE (proportion units)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

moe_ratio_sf <- moe_df |>
  dplyr::left_join(tracts_sf, by = "GEOID") |>
  sf::st_as_sf()

ratio_lim <- max(abs(moe_df$ratio - 1), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(moe_ratio_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = ratio), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette  = "RdBu",
    limits   = c(1 - ratio_lim, 1 + ratio_lim),
    name     = "MOE ratio\n(TW / ACS)",
    na.value = "grey80"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "MOE ratio: TWDeConv 2020 vs. ACS 2018\u20132022",
    subtitle = "Blue (<1) = TWDeConv more precise; Red (>1) = ACS more precise  |  St. Louis City tracts"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9)
  )
